name: Acetryptine
summary: Acetryptine is a drug described as an antihypertensive agent which was never marketed. Structurally, acetryptine is a substituted tryptamine, and is closely related to other substituted tryptamines like serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine). It was developed in the early 1960s.

pharmacology.text: The binding of acetryptine to serotonin receptors does not seem to have been well-investigated, although it was assessed at the 5-HT1A and 5-HT1D receptors and found to bind to them with high affinity. The drug may also act as a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI); specifically, as an inhibitor of MAO-A.

uses.text: Acetryptine (INN; developmental code W-2965-A; also known as 5-acetyltryptamine or 5-AT) is a drug described as an antihypertensive agent which was never marketed. The binding of acetryptine to serotonin receptors does not seem to have been well-investigated, although it was assessed at the 5-HT1A and 5-HT1D receptors and found to bind to them with high affinity.

sideEffects.en: Little is known about it in people. It was never marketed, and no reliable account of its effects in people exists.
sideEffects.zh: 目前對它在人體的作用所知甚少。它從未上市，也沒有關於它在人體作用的可靠紀錄。
sideEffects.zhHans: 目前对它在人体的作用所知甚少。它从未上市，也没有关于它在人体作用的可靠纪录。

fact.en: It was developed in the early 1960s as a possible blood pressure medicine, an unusual aim for a tryptamine, and it was never brought to market.
fact.zh: 它在1960年代初期作為可能的降血壓藥開發，這對一種色胺來說是個不尋常的目標，而它始終沒有上市。
fact.zhHans: 它在1960年代初期作为可能的降血压药开发，这对一种色胺来说是个不寻常的目标，而它始终没有上市。
